newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait to shed Public Warehousing stake.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait to shed Public Warehousing stake.

text.p: Kuwait plans to sell 120 million shares of its Public Warehousing Co holdings in two stages, a firm managing part of the sale said on Sunday.
Kuwait Clearing Company will hold an auction on behalf of the Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA), the state investment arm, to sell 40 million shares on April 4, a company official said.
KIA has set 384 fils ($1.27) as a starting price for the auction, he said. The share closed at 440 fils on Saturday. There are 1,000 fils to the dinar.
Another 80 million shares will be sold in a public offering at a date and a price to be set by KIA after the auction.
Total state stake in the 18-year-old firm amounts to 49 percent of its 269.34 million issued shares.
Public Warehousing's net profit rose 16.5 percent to 5.45 million dinars in 1996. Dividends rose 14.3 percent to 16 fils per share.
Only nationals of the Gulf Cooperation Council countries -- Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Bahrian, the United Arab Emirates, Oman and Qatar -- can trade shares of Kuwaiti firms.
